newsitem.title: USA: Delta employees held in Puerto Rico cocaine case.
newsitem.headline: Delta employees held in Puerto Rico cocaine case.

text.p: Twelve members of a drug trafficking ring, most of whom are past or current employees of Delta Air Lines, were indicted on charges that they smuggled cocaine through Puerto Rico into the United States, U.S. officials said on Wednesday.

The organisation shipped hundreds of pounds (kilos) of Colombian cocaine through the Puerto Rican capital San Juan's Luis Munoz Marin International Airport, Drug Enforcement Administration special agent Felix Jimenez said.
Nine of those indicted were arrested on Wednesday and three are still being sought.

"We are aware that some Delta employees were arrested in conjunction with illegal drug activity. We cooperated fully with the DEA in this ivestigation," Delta spokeswoman Kim King told Reuters in Atlanta.
Jimenez said the Delta employees used their positions in the airline industry to put cocaine-filled suitcases and cargo containers on board Delta aircraft.
"What is important is that this was airline employees," he told Reuters in a telephone interview. "This is the first time we have had an organised ring operating like that."
Seven of those indicted were arrested in Puerto Rico. One was taken into custody in Orlando, Florida, and the other in Cincinnati, Ohio.
Jimenez said the DEA was called in by Delta on Sept. 21, 1995 when three crates arrived at the Delta cargo terminal.
"One of the people handling them appeared very nervous, an indication that something was wrong," he said. "The organisation was responsible for passing the cocaine through airport security."
DEA agents seized 1,137 pounds (517 kg) and "attempted to make a controlled delivery to New York. The attempt was aborted because it was compromised," he said.
Agents then traced the cocaine back and "infiltrated Delta airlines employees responsible for smuggling the cocaine."
Three weeks ago a federal grand jury returned an indictment on the 12 people, all of whom are Puerto Rican.
"The cocaine was coming from Colombia. Virtually all the cocaine we seize in Puerto Rico comes from Colombia," Jimenez said.
